newsitem.title: UK: UK public deficit may be structural -Labour.
newsitem.headline: UK public deficit may be structural -Labour.

text.p: Public borrowing figures published on Tuesday expose the hollowness of British government claims that its finances are under control, the opposition Labour Party said.
The figures showed a 4.53 billion stg public sector borrowing requirement in August which took the total PSBR for the first five months of the current financial year to 13.37 billion stg.

"Today's figures are depressingly familiar. They show just how hollow are the Government's claims that the public finances are back on track," said Alistair Darling, the shadow chief secretary to the treasury.
He said that since 1990, the national debt had doubled and the government had never meet its borrowing targets since the 1992 general election.
"These figures...suggest that the deficit may be structural. They reinforce Labour's call for a full independent audit of the state of the public finances," Darling said in a statement.
